messages.content: 尋找紐約附近提供素食選項的義大利餐廳，以及洛杉磯提供外送服務的日本壽司餐廳。

function.name: restaurant_finder
function.description: Search for restaurants based on location, cuisine type and other preferences. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: City and state, e.g. New York, NY.

cuisine.description: Type of cuisine the user is interested in, e.g. Italian, Japanese etc.

preferences.description: Extra features in the restaurant. default is ['Delivery'].

message.reasoning:
The user wants two searches:

1. In New York (NY) find Italian restaurants with vegetarian options.

2. In Los Angeles (LA) find Japanese sushi restaurants with delivery service.

We need to call the function twice. The function signature: restaurant_finder takes location, cuisine, preferences optional array of strings. For first: location: "New York, NY", cuisine: "Italian", preferences: ["Vegetarian"]. For second: location: "Los Angeles, CA" (or "Los Angeles, CA"? The user said Los Angeles; we can use "Los Angeles, CA"), cuisine: "Japanese", preferences: ["Delivery"].

We need to output the function calls. According to guidelines, we should not provide additional text besides the function calls. So we will produce two separate function calls. The format: JSON object with name and arguments. We need to produce them as separate messages? The guidelines say: "When calling a function, you must respond with a JSON object containing the name of the function and arguments." It doesn't specify multiple calls in one response. But we can do two separate responses. However, the system might expect only one function call per assistant turn. But we can combine them into one? The guidelines say "When calling a function, you must respond with a JSON object containing the name of the function and arguments." That implies each function call is a separate response. But we have two queries. We could call the function twice sequentially. But the user asked for both. We can do two separate calls. But the guidelines also say "If you want to call a function, you must respond with a JSON object containing the name of the function and arguments." So we can produce two separate messages: first call for New York, second call for Los Angeles. That seems acceptable.

Thus we produce:

First message: {"name":"restaurant_finder","arguments":{"location":"New York, NY","cuisine":"Italian","preferences":["Vegetarian"]}}

Second message: {"name":"restaurant_finder","arguments":{"location":"Los Angeles, CA","cuisine":"Japanese","preferences":["Delivery"]}}

We should not add any extra text.
